This suggests that simply adjusting reward weights does not reliably induce the intended prioritization when the underlying objectives differ substantially in difficulty. Only when w length w_{\text{length}} is reduced to 0.25, making it sufficiently small to compensate for the difficulty gap between the objectives, do we observe a clear increase in the length-exceeding ratio on AIME for both GRPO and GDPO and on MATH for GDPO. We next investigate whether conditioning the easier length reward on the more challenging correctness reward can help mitigate the disparity in difficulty between the two objectives and help improve priority alignment.
